tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the Recurly sites the API key can see (subdomain, live or sandbox mode)

state.description: Optional site state to filter by

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: List Recurly accounts (customers), optionally filtered by exact email address

email.description: Optional exact email address to filter by (multiple accounts can share one)

subscriber.description: Optional: true for accounts with an active, canceled or future subscription, false for those without

tools.name: list_subscriptions
tools.description: List Recurly subscriptions, optionally filtered by state

state.description: Optional subscription state to filter by

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: List Recurly invoices, optionally filtered by state and invoice type

state.description: Optional invoice state to filter by (Recurly defaults to all)

type.description: Optional invoice type to filter by

needs_review: auth left as scaffolded (basic, api_key as the username, empty password) because Recurly's own OpenAPI proves it right: securityScheme api_key is { type: http, scheme: basic } with the description 'Enter the API key as the username and set the password to an empty string'. passField '' is the documented empty password, not a placeholder.

the Accept version header is REQUIRED, not decorative: Recurly's v3 API selects its API version from the Accept header, documented as 'Accept: application/vnd.recurly.v2021-02-25'. static_headers pins v2021-02-25, which is the version of the spec every path and every picked field below was read from. Changing that string without re-reading the spec would silently change response shapes.

base_url is the US host v3.recurly.com. Recurly's OpenAPI lists a second server, https://v3.eu.recurly.com, for EU-hosted sites; a customer on the EU region will fail against this spec, and spec v1 cannot pick a host per credential without a base_url template field the vault does not carry.

tools_source is Recurly's OFFICIAL published OpenAPI document (linked from the redoc reference at recurly.com/developers/api/v2021-02-25/index.html), so every path, every query parameter, every enum and every picked field name is taken verbatim from it rather than from prose.
READ-ONLY by design: no tool is marked write:true. The v3 API has create/update/delete endpoints for accounts, subscriptions, invoices, purchases and refunds; none is modelled.

limit is clamped 20/200 exactly as documented ('Limit number of records 1-200', default 20). Lists answer the envelope { object, has_more, next, data[] }, so has_more and next are picked: next is the cursor URL a caller would follow, and the declarative runtime cannot follow it, so a caller sees at most one page per call.

every picked field name is taken verbatim from the v2021-02-25 schemas (Site, Account = AccountReadOnly + AccountResponse, Subscription with AccountMini/PlanMini children, Invoice), NOT from a live 2xx: the shape-proof stops at 401, so no body was ever data. A wrong pick source yields empty output silently, so the first run with a real key must confirm them.

deliberately NOT picked: Account.billing_info and Invoice.line_items / transactions / credit_payments. Billing info carries payment-instrument detail and the nested collections are unbounded, so both would inflate an LLM context for little gain. Invoice.address and shipping_address are omitted for the same privacy reason as the Gusto PII exclusion.

list_accounts exposes email and subscriber but not past_due, begin_time or end_time: the time filters are only meaningful together with an explicit sort field, which this spec does not expose, so offering them alone would mislead.
rateLimit 30/min is a local courtesy and spend guard chosen here; Recurly publishes its own per-key ceilings (documented separately per environment) and this is not a quote of them.

shape-proof 2026-09-12 is overall SHAPE_PROVEN, runner line verbatim: 'recurly  SHAPE_PROVEN  proven=5 authwall=0 ambiguous=0 failed=0 inconclusive=0 skipped=0'. All five real calls (/sites twice, as test and as tool, plus /accounts, /subscriptions and /invoices) answer 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header and the structured JSON body {"error":{"type":"unauthorized","message":"Invalid API key"}}, while the bogus control path answers 404 with Recurly's HTML 'Page Not Found - Recurly' page rather than an API envelope, so host, TLS, base_url, basic auth, the Accept version header and every route are proven distinct from the control. What the proof does NOT cover: no response body was ever data, so the picks above rest on the published OpenAPI, and the EU-region host is unprobed.
